Reviewed the complete claim, both implementation entries and complete test set. This accepts explicitly deferred work, not full implemented behavior. The obligations are non-ground termination and sound knowledge (allowing ambiguity despite available instantiations), complete ground answers unless named deterministic limits exhaust, and separate incomplete-source, ambiguity and overflow outcomes which never become No. The captured architectural rationale counts rigid placeholders as ground and names depth, canonical-term-size, logical-work and fixpoint limits.

The ordinary solve_query entry validates the query, imports proof state, drives a whiteboard, asserts branch cleanup and extracts the result. Direct control flow in the captured prove.rs checks MAX_PROOF_DEPTH in prove_atom and returns Maybe on exhaustion. Whiteboard keys include remaining depth; an identical ancestor currently returns No via the provisional inductive cutoff. Candidate tasks import separate state, extract responses and discard children. solve_trait_frame passes its incomplete flag to the merger. These observations establish scaffolding, not a proof of helper behavior or complete soundness. The depth guard does not itself return No, but its Maybe does not distinguish exhaustion from ambiguity. Complete ground solving and the resource taxonomy are not implemented by this entry point.

The associated sage_meta::todo implementation explicitly documents that ground completeness and the full deterministic resource taxonomy remain planned. The only associated test, solver_bounded_completeness, is correctly TODO and has no executable assertions. Its matrix explicitly covers ground positive/negative answers, non-ground ambiguity despite an instantiation, incomplete sources, every configured limit class, repeated canonical outcomes, and no false No on incomplete/exhausted cases. Its prerequisite is implementing the missing ground-completeness and named resource/outcome machinery, then executing this matrix including sound non-ground results and termination. This is an honest deferred verification plan, not behavioral coverage. A collapse of overflow into ambiguity would evade this empty test; this review does not claim otherwise. No N/A entries exist. The explicit implementation and test TODOs account for the remaining requirements, and remain deferred.

Captured context includes complete associated files/test, review policy and architectural rationale. No Rust source was edited and no behavioral tests or workspace build were run by this reviewer. Only review start/read/record commands were executed. No edits are requested because the documented deferral remains accurate.
